/-!
# Conjecture 5.54

by J. Wiegold

Let $p, q, r$ be distinct primes and $u(x, y, z)$ a commutator word in three
variables. Prove that there exist (infinitely many?) natural numbers $n$ such
that the alternating group $\mathbb{A}_n$ can be generated by three elements
$\xi, \eta, \zeta$ satisfying
$\xi^p = \eta^q = \zeta^r = \xi \eta \zeta \cdot u(\xi, \eta, \zeta) = 1$.

A commutator word in three variables is an element of the derived subgroup
$F' = [F, F]$ of the free group $F$ on $x, y, z$. It is formalised as an element
`u` of `commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3))`, and $u(\xi, \eta, \zeta)$ is the image
of `u` under `FreeGroup.lift ![ξ, η, ζ]`.

Only the existence claim is formalised. The parenthetical question of whether
there are infinitely many such $n$ for every choice of $p, q, r, u$ has a
trivial negative answer: for $p, q, r = 2, 3, 5$ and $u = 1$ the relations
define the triangle group $\Delta(2, 3, 5) \cong \mathbb{A}_5$, so only $n = 5$
works.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.54» (p q r : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime)
    (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r)
    (u : FreeGroup (Fin 3)) (hu : u ∈ commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3))) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 5 ≤ n ∧ ∃ ξ η ζ : alternatingGroup (Fin n),
      Subgroup.closure {ξ, η, ζ} = ⊤ ∧
      ξ ^ p = 1 ∧ η ^ q = 1 ∧ ζ ^ r = 1 ∧
      ξ * η * ζ * FreeGroup.lift ![ξ, η, ζ] u = 1 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $p, q, r$ be distinct primes and $u(x, y, z)$ a commutator word in three
variables. Then there exists a natural number $n$ such that the alternating
group $\mathbb{A}_n$ can be generated by three elements $\xi, \eta, \zeta$
satisfying $\xi^p = \eta^q = \zeta^r = \xi \eta \zeta \cdot u(\xi, \eta, \zeta) = 1$.

The restriction $n \geq 5$ excludes the degenerate values $n \leq 2$, for which
$\mathbb{A}_n$ is trivial and $\xi = \eta = \zeta = 1$ satisfies every relation.
It excludes nothing else: since $p, q, r$ are distinct primes and $u$ is a
commutator word, the relations force the group generated by $\xi, \eta, \zeta$
to be perfect, which rules out $\mathbb{A}_3$ and $\mathbb{A}_4$.

claims.decomposer_note: Primary claim: for ALL distinct primes p,q,r and EVERY commutator word u (an element of the derived subgroup of the free group on x,y,z — some read it more narrowly as a single commutator [v,w]) there EXISTS n with A_n a quotient of ⟨x,y,z | x^p, y^q, z^r, xyz·u(x,y,z)⟩ via generators ξ,η,ζ; stated as 'Prove that', so no answer(sorry); the formalization must exclude the degenerate witnesses n ≤ 2 (A_n trivial, so ξ=η=ζ=1 satisfies every relation) e.g. by requiring n ≥ 5 (A_n simple) or that ξ,η,ζ have orders exactly p,q,r.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot essentially identically (u ∈ commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3)), ξ η ζ : alternatingGroup (Fin n), Subgroup.closure {ξ,η,ζ} = ⊤, ξ^p = η^q = ζ^r = 1, ξ*η*ζ*FreeGroup.lift ![ξ,η,ζ] u = 1, plain theorem with no answer(sorry) since the source says 'Prove that'). c04's version was taken: hypotheses as named binders (matching Kourovka file style), bound 5 ≤ n, and a docstring that correctly explains why the bound excludes exactly the degenerate n ≤ 2 (the presented group is perfect because p,q,r are distinct primes and u ∈ F', so A_3, A_4 are never witnesses). c01's 3 ≤ n is mathematically equivalent; c02/c06/c07/c08 are the same statement with ∀-binders; c03 wraps it in a bespoke predicate that adds nothing. Verified in Lean that FreeGroup.lift ![ξ,η,ζ] sends of 0/1/2 to ξ/η/ζ and that n = 0 is a degenerate witness without the bound. Docstring lightly edited; module docstring records the omission of the parenthetical.
claims.source_text: Prove that there exist (infinitely many?) natural numbers $n$ such that the alternating group ${\Bbb A}_n$ can be generated by three elements $\xi , \eta , \zeta$ satisfying $\xi ^p= \eta ^q= \zeta ^r=\xi \eta \zeta \cdot u(\xi , \eta , \zeta )=1$
claims.text_span: Prove that there exist (infinitely many?) natural numbers $n$ such that the alternating group ${\Bbb A}_n$ can be generated by three elements $\xi , \eta , \zeta$ satisfying $\xi ^p= \eta ^q= \zeta ^r=\xi \eta \zeta \cdot u(\xi , \eta , \zeta )=1$

claims.decomposer_note: Stronger form posed as a question (so answer(sorry) ↔ … is appropriate): for all distinct primes p,q,r and every commutator word u, the set of n with A_n generated by such ξ,η,ζ is infinite (Set.Infinite / ∀ N ∃ n > N); the degenerate small-n witnesses do not trivialize this version, but same commutator-word ambiguity applies.
claims.reviewer_why: Omitted. Every candidate states it as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ distinct primes p q r, ∀ u ∈ F', Set.Infinite {n | …}. As c01 flagged, this literal universal statement has a trivial negative answer: for (p,q,r) = (2,3,5) and u = 1 (which lies in the derived subgroup under every reading, and equals the commutator [x,x]) the relations present the triangle group Δ(2,3,5) ≅ A_5, so the witness set is {0,1,2,5}, finite. Requiring u ≠ 1 does not help: u = [xyz, x] is a nontrivial single commutator and xyz·[xyz,x] = x⁻¹(xyz)x, so the relation again collapses to xyz = 1 and the same counterexample applies. Hence shipping it as 'research open' would list a question whose formal answer is already determined (False) by a degenerate instance, contrary to STATEMENTS.md's boundary-case rule; shipping it as 'research solved, answer(False)' would misrepresent the source, which records it as open. Any hypothesis that would rescue the intended question (e.g. that the presented group be infinite, or 1/p+1/q+1/r < 1) is not in the source and could not be justified as the author's intent, so the slot cannot be stated faithfully.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's two slots (existence as 'Prove that', infinitude as a question) match the source text, and its note about excluding degenerate n ≤ 2 witnesses is correct; I chose the n ≥ 5 option and verified it excludes exactly the degenerate cases (A_3, A_4 are not perfect while the presented group is).

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.54» (p q r : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hr : r.Prime)
    (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r) (hqr : q ≠ r)
    (u : FreeGroup (Fin 3)) (hu : u ∈ commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3))) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 5 ≤ n ∧ ∃ ξ η ζ : alternatingGroup (Fin n),
      Subgroup.closure {ξ, η, ζ} = ⊤ ∧
      ξ ^ p = 1 ∧ η ^ q = 1 ∧ ζ ^ r = 1 ∧
      ξ * η * ζ * FreeGroup.lift ![ξ, η, ζ] u = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.54»

items: 'Commutator word in three variables' is read as an element of the derived subgroup [F,F] of the free group F on x,y,z (H. Neumann / Wiegold usage), formalised as `u ∈ commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3))`. This is the broader reading in the decomposition table; the narrower 'single commutator [v,w]' reading is a special case, so the stated theorem implies the narrow one.
u(ξ,η,ζ) is `FreeGroup.lift ![ξ, η, ζ] u`, i.e. x ↦ ξ (index 0), y ↦ η (index 1), z ↦ ζ (index 2). Since u ranges over all of [F,F], the index convention is immaterial.

'Generated by three elements ξ, η, ζ' is `Subgroup.closure {ξ, η, ζ} = ⊤` inside the group `alternatingGroup (Fin n)`; ξ, η, ζ are not required to be distinct or nontrivial (the source's relations ξ^p = 1 etc. do not require exact orders either).

Primary slot adds `5 ≤ n` to exclude the degenerate witnesses n ≤ 2 (A_n trivial, ξ=η=ζ=1 satisfies everything). This is equivalent to only excluding n ≤ 2: the group ⟨x,y,z | x^p,y^q,z^r,xyz·u⟩ is perfect (its abelianization is (ℤ_p×ℤ_q×ℤ_r)/⟨(1,1,1)⟩ = 1 because p,q,r are distinct primes and u ∈ F'), so A_3 and A_4, which are not perfect, are never witnesses. The docstring explains this restriction.
The infinitude variant is stated literally without the n-bound, since finitely many degenerate witnesses cannot change `Set.Infinite`.
Distinctness of p,q,r is encoded as the three inequalities p ≠ q, p ≠ r, q ≠ r; primality via Nat.Prime.
Category `research open` for both slots, AMS 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: 'commutator word' was read (as all candidates and the decomposition table's primary reading) as an element of the derived subgroup of the free group on x,y,z, i.e. `commutator (FreeGroup (Fin 3))`; the narrower single-commutator reading is a special case, so the shipped existence claim implies the narrow one. The relations are kept literal (ξ^p = 1 etc.), not exact orders; degenerate trivial A_n (n ≤ 2, where ξ=η=ζ=1 works) are excluded by 5 ≤ n, which is exactly equivalent to excluding n ≤ 2 because the presented group ⟨x,y,z | x^p,y^q,z^r,xyz·u⟩ is perfect for distinct primes and u ∈ F' (abelianization (ℤ_p×ℤ_q×ℤ_r)/⟨(1,1,1)⟩ = 1), while A_3, A_4 are not perfect. The 'infinitely many?' variant is omitted for the reason given per slot: the decomposition table's note that degenerate cases 'do not trivialize this version' is incorrect — the degeneracy is not small n but the spherical triple (2,3,5) with u = 1 (or u = [xyz,g]), which makes the universal infinitude statement false; c01 correctly flagged this while the other seven candidates shipped it unflagged. The module docstring records this omission briefly so a contributor understands the scope. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
